I've been working this land in Quzhou my whole life — sixty years of farming, more or less. I know this soil. I know this weather. My sons moved to the city, so mostly it is just me now, with help during busy periods.

Around here, everyone grows winter wheat and summer maize on the same plots, rotating them year after year. That is what I will do too. I have about 6 mu that I manage myself. My wheat goes in October, comes out in June. Then I turn around and put in maize right away on the same ground, harvest it in September. This rhythm I have followed my whole life and I see no reason to change it.

For wheat, I will use the improved variety seed from the county supply cooperative — not the old landrace my father grew, but not the expensive hybrid either. I will plough the field before sowing the way I always do. I will put down compound fertilizer at planting and come back with urea after the spring green-up. I water three times: once when I plant, once before it freezes, and once when the stems are stretching. I spray twice — once for weeds early on, once later when the aphids come, which they always do.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed. Everyone does now and the yield is better. After I cut the wheat I run the rotary tiller over the stalks and plant the same week. Maize mostly feeds on the summer rains, but if tasseling comes dry I will pump one irrigation. I push the nitrogen on maize — it is hungry crop. One herbicide pass early is enough.
